A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A-E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Random Hierarchy Model data, OpenWebText, and ImageNet64, together with representation-sensitivity, clustering, and perplexity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with revised checkpoint coverage in the natural-data results.

M1.justification: The D3PM U-Net, hierarchical clustering procedures, and natural-data diffusion models are retained. Section 4.3 explains context-vector construction more explicitly without establishing a change to the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate hierarchical grammar generation using the RHM, text generation on OpenWebText, and image generation on ImageNet64. No dataset, domain, or distinct task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figures 2 and 7 retain the same clustering comparisons based on a single visible token or an entire visible tuple. Figure 8 retains the OpenWebText validation reference. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation grid changes: Figure 4 includes different intermediate language-model checkpoints, and Figure 5 adds two image-model checkpoints. The metrics, overall training budgets, architectures, and per-checkpoint generation sample counts remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish retraining.

E4.justification: The synonym-sensitivity analysis, deeper clustering experiment, context-dependent perplexity analysis, and generated examples in Appendices D-E are retained. The new threshold-robustness footnote does not document an additional sweep or provide supporting test results.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same correlation sampling-noise references and 1024-sample perplexity averaging. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 4 replaces the 6.71e7- and 2.68e8-token curves with newly reported curves at approximately 5.4e8, 7.6e8, 1.3e9, and 1.5e9 tokens. Shared checkpoint curves are retained, with rounded legend values. Figure 5 adds two intermediate MMD checkpoint results. The staged-learning findings and appendix results remain stable.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 explicitly defines the score as a log-density gradient and distinguishes it from conditional-mean prediction, replacing v1's unqualified proportionality statement. Section 4.2 incorporates the factor 1/(1-m/v^(s-1)) into its sample-complexity expressions. This factor already appeared in v1's appendix mathematics; the underlying assumptions and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion identify the RHM or simple-grammar setting more explicitly, narrowing previously broader wording about hierarchical data. The conclusion additionally claims explanatory relevance to diffusion-model hallucination findings. The central polynomial sample-complexity and progressively increasing coherence claims remain.

C2.justification: Sections 3.2 and 6 more explicitly interpret natural-data behavior as support for generality beyond the RHM and connect the mechanism to hallucinations. Section 3.3 adds a threshold-robustness assertion. Section 4.2 removes the qualification about a possible weight-sharing-dependent 1/d factor and the focus on m much larger than s.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies constructing context vectors by averaging neighboring one-hot tokens, expressed as E[x | h = nu], before k-means clustering. Appendix C retains the implementation settings, hardware information, and code sources; the shortened Improved DDPM URL identifies the same repository.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations concerning geometric inductive bias, compositional learning, hierarchical feature emergence, and hallucinations, including Kadkhodaie et al. (2023b), Park et al. (2024), Li and Chen (2024), Lu et al. (2025), and Han et al. (2025). Chomsky et al. (1976) supports the creativity framing. The main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract and introduction, expands explanations of diffusion notation, representation probing, and clustering, and revises the conclusion. The section sequence and appendix organization remain substantially unchanged. Publication metadata and terminology also receive limited updates.

P2.justification: Figure 3 redraws the RHM tree with explicit rule nodes and an updated caption. Figure 4 changes its curve set, colors, and legend. Several figures move with text reflow, and conference-style headers and a supplementary-material heading are introduced. Most figure designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Clearer clustering instructions, more precise identification of the RHM setting, and better alignment of main-text formulas with existing appendix derivations modestly improve clarity and reproducibility. Additional checkpoints resolve the learning transitions more finely. These gains are limited: Figure 4's caption still refers to an omitted early checkpoint, and the weight-sharing qualification is removed.
